note: Legal record for the SOURCE tree redistributed inside the package (waft-src/), kept SEPARATE from the conda runtime license inventory. The Andrew Miller runtime legal-review approves ONLY the conda runtime (legal/runtime-license-inventory.json); it does NOT cover redistributed source. This record covers the source and is bound into the package by scripts/ci-waft-validation-qualify.sh, which stages each component's authoritative licence text under legal/source/ and fails closed if a carried component's licence text is missing.

components.note: The pinned WAFT source's own root LICENSE (BSD-3-Clause) travels inside the clean git checkout; CI asserts its presence when vendoring.

components.notice_note: The upstream Depth-Anything-V2 repository has NO NOTICE file (verified: contents/NOTICE returns HTTP 404), so none is staged.
components.reason: WAFT vendors thirdparty/DepthAnythingV2 as tracked code (NOT a git submodule) that model/backbone/vit.py imports at module scope, so the subtree is redistributed inside waft-src/. Its Python source headers declare Apache-2.0, but the subtree ships NO LICENSE file and WAFT's only root LICENSE is BSD-3-Clause -- so copying the checkout would redistribute Apache-2.0 source without its licence text. The authoritative Apache-2.0 text is therefore staged separately under legal/source/ and bound here, WITHOUT writing into the vendored tree (which would dirty the checkout and export_waft.py's git rev-parse/clean-worktree gate would reject it).

source.retrieval_note: Fetched by git blob SHA1 261eeb9e9f8b2b4b0d119366dda99c6fd7d35c64 from the DepthAnything/Depth-Anything-V2 repository (default branch main at commit a561b849ebae10a6f5ef49e26c83cbbcd36c71bf). The bytes are the unmodified canonical Apache License 2.0 text (its blob SHA1 261eeb9e... is the well-known hash of the standard LICENSE; the appendix carries the generic 'Copyright [yyyy] [name of copyright owner]' placeholder, i.e. upstream ships the stock text unaltered).
